source_text:
BTW while we wait it could be interesting to write up a summary cover note to send to Aleks Kissinger in connection with his newly funded project Teaching theorem provers to understand diagrams
This project integrates diagrammatic reasoning, a radically different way of understanding and manipulating complex compositional systems, into mainstream interactive theorem provers. The theory behind diagrammatic reasoning is well understood and prototype tools exist, but significant technical and interface challenges remain, so the project translates it into the dependent type theory spoken by Rocq and Lean, develops automated tactics that allow a prover to understand and manipulate diagrams, and builds an interface that makes co-creating a proof with the machine visual, intuitive, and engaging. Two case studies will demonstrate the formalism — one based on the ZX-calculus, a well-established graphical language for quantum computation, and one on graphical algebraic geometry, a newly introduced formalism for reasoning compositionally about polynomial ideals and varieties — alongside an assessment of how well AI tools can co-develop rigorous diagrammatic proofs.

reply_text:
I'll read the DiagramProver mission and the related Lean/futon6 work before drafting, so the note cites what exists.Patching the diagrams paragraph with the Simmons–Kissinger citation and the three open questions the Dark Tower note already meant to carry to him, then committing the draft.㊥ (gist) A draft is written and committed, in your voice, ready for you to cut and send:

```
futon3c/holes/labs/M-diagramprover/NOTE-cover-note-kissinger-2026-10-13.md
```

Open it and read from "Dear Aleks" down. Below the letter is a list of where each figure comes from.

㊢ (what it says) It meets the project at its four parts in turn. DiagramProver: the 489-problem curriculum corpus, the April run's numbers, tactic traces as string diagrams with goal-state types as ports. Formal requirements first: the 238 War Machine Lean files as the specification the code conforms to. Where diagrams meet our mathematics: the Dark Tower notes already build on Simmons and Kissinger's Caus[𝒞] and BV paper, and the June grounding pass left three underdetermined items that were written down as "questions to carry to Kissinger" and never sent, so the letter asks them. The futon6 dependency graph with its review buffer as a corpus-and-review loop for the graphical algebraic geometry case study. And the co-creation assessment, where the labelled dialogue grammar and author-not-reviewer reviewing are what we have to offer.

㊟ (things to check before sending) The three conjecture questions are taken from the 2026-06-12 checkpoint in the second Dark Tower note; you may want to reread that section and decide whether they are the questions you would ask him today. The proof-landscape numbers are from April and say so. I left out mfuton, since the shared repository is Rob's and the Lean parser work is his to describe, and I named no collaborators.
